newsitem.title: TURKEY: Kurd MP vows to reveal more in Turkish scandal.
newsitem.headline: Kurd MP vows to reveal more in Turkish scandal.

text.p: A Kurdish MP and warlord at the centre of a row over alleged links between Turkey's powerful security apparatus and far-right gangsters has threatened to reveal more details of the scandal.
Government MP Sedat Bucak said in remarks published on Thursday he would name names in the ruling elite who had ties to late fugitive mobster Abdullah Catli.

"There were a lot of people who knew Catli," the Gozcu newspaper quoted Bucak as saying in an interview. "If I get up and speak -- and I will speak when the time is right -- I don't know what they are going to do," he said.
Kurdish tribal chief Bucak acknowledged a close friendship with Catli, a suspected heroin smuggler wanted for the murder of seven leftist militants in the late 1970s.

"I loved him as one loves a big brother," Bucak said in his first public comments since a fatal crash earlier this month that raised still unanswered questions about possible ties between leading officials and the right-wing underworld.
Bucak was the only survivor from a car carrying Catli, a senior policeman and a former beauty queen that crashed in western Turkey.
Bucak said the policemen did not know the true identity of Catli, who was carrying a false passport of a type only issued to top officials.
The scandal forced then interior minister Mehmet Agar to resign.
Bucak, who heads a tribal militia that fights Kurdish rebels in southeast Turkey, was photographed by the newspaper at his MP's residence looking dishevelled and with a plaster cast on his right leg.
The MP said that seven guns found in the car belonged to him but he denied any knowlege of two silencers recovered from the wreckage.
"Everyone knows about my struggle against the (Kurdistan Workers Party) PKK. There may well have been weapons in the car but no silencers," he said.
Bucak, a member of the junior coalition partner True Path Party (DYP), has not been questioned by police about the crash.

But six of his bodyguards were quizzed by a prosecutor on Wednesday about allegations in the press that they were involved in the murder in Istanbul of "Casino King" Omer Lutfu Topal earlier this year.
The media has said that Bucak's men killed the casino owner, alleged to have given money to the PKK, in a battle over laundered money from the heroin trade.
